Critique of S2.2 (security-reviewer), hostile, limited to the three claims and the 18.0 threat model. Read: lib/greenfield/index.js, runner.js, run-check.js, closure.js (accept, acceptanceProblems, openFindings), bin/eccode-gf.js, tests/gf-review-s2-h2.test.js, gf-runner-copy.test.js, gf-accept.test.js, and to follow the paths: lib/mcp.js (the whole tool table), lib/evidence.js, lib/tasks.js (staged verification), lib/worktree.js, lib/guards/*.js, lib/security.js, lib/install.js (giveRoleTools), scripts/hooks/guard.js (the MCP branch), lib/util.js (withLock, spawnGrouped). Reproductions are in review-i/ and were run from my clone.

WHAT I ATTACKED AND WHAT HELD

H2-1, the refusal. The eight COMMAND_TOOLS are refused per call (index.js:107-114) to every role C.groupOf puts in a group, only when wrap.isEnabled says the record is Greenfield-Senior, before the frozen handler runs, so nothing is recorded; the orchestrator and no-group roles keep them. Being decided per call covers a project that becomes Greenfield-Senior after the server starts; an unreadable record makes isEnabled throw, which fails closed (the tool does not run). gf_battery_run checks the orchestrator before running anything (closure.js:345); quick/debug/task_rescope cannot add a pinned command for a group role. That part held.

H2-1, the pinned run. The runner records extra.command = the trimmed command it accepted (runner.js:205), the frozen staged-verification compares whitespace-normalised commands (tasks.js:253-254) and accepts only status passed, which the wrapper's exit 99 (outside change, copy error) prevents. A pinned form records its own words, so a scoped form cannot stand for a different pinned command; a plan-pinned command is matched whole and recorded as pinned. The log's first line and runner.executed keep the wrapper line. Held.

H2-2. RESTORED (run-check.js:30) is anchored to the top-level events.jsonl, state.json, config.json, .lock and .lock.waiting-*; drafts, evidence logs, guard configs and artifacts are hashed. A legitimate single run is not failed by the engine itself: the frozen runner holds .eccode/.lock for the whole run and writes the run's own log only after the child exits (evidence.js:98-112). In-model relative writes to .eccode/ land in the copy, which has no .eccode, and are discarded and listed. I found no in-model write into .eccode/ that passes the runner's check. Held.

GF-CLOSE-6. acceptanceProblems matches the paragraph: actor user, clean tree, neither closed nor already accepted, every open finding exactly once with its recorded severity, L-GF-<n> and a 30+ character reason, nothing else, none blocking, not empty, judged at its own seq; there is no MCP tool; the audit replays it and reports valid ones as accepted. It accepts a scope that has open findings and also a missing review step or a standing no-go (tests/gf-accept.test.js:47 accepts with no readiness review). That matches the conditions and is the documentation ambiguity I recorded as I1-1 in my comprehension review; I do not count it again here.

WHAT BROKE

I2-1 (blocking, engine behavior, review-i/i2-1-guard-tools.test.js). The runner is not the only route. guard_migration (proof), security_matrix/idor/authflow/input, guard_api, guard_perf and guard_race are tools of every role's server (the installer grants all tools; the hook checks only the server name), they are not in COMMAND_TOOLS, and they run project commands and project code (the configured seed/upgrade/downgrade, the configured setup, the app import) through evidence.runCommand in a git worktree of the real repository whose .venv/node_modules/venv/vendor are symlinks to the real tree, under the frozen windows only. The engine's own delivery messages tell the owner (a group role) to run them. As database-engineer, both demonstrated tools let the db group's code write another group's draft and a frontend path by absolute path and the real .venv by a relative path; nothing is refused or failed, and security_matrix reports success. The same seed through gf_run fails with exit 99 (control, same file). behavior_diff is the same kind of tool but is refused on the greenfield track (TRACK_RULE), so it does not apply.

OUTSIDE THE SCOPE (for the limits register)
1. A forged gf.slice.accepted (written past the CLI, L-GF-17) still counts as "already accepted" (closure.js:380 does not filter invalid acceptances), so it blocks the owner's real acceptance although the table says a forged one "stands for nothing". It needs a forged event, which is outside the model.
2. The guard and security tools pass undeclared arguments through (the server does not check arguments against the schema), so a caller can name its own interpreter (python) for the probe. That is deliberate misuse, not an LLM-plausible mistake.
3. A background process left running by the command can write the real tree between the wrapper's second hash and the frozen runner's process-group kill (the copy-back window). Not reproduced.
4. Concurrency: with .eccode/ hashed, another agent's legitimate write there during a run (its group's draft under .eccode/drafts/<group>/, which the hook allows; a memory record and its nested .lock; a handoff written after the lock is released) fails the run, as the text says ("as if the run had made it; the remedy is to run again"). Since S2.1 the same was already true for other groups' source files. This is a liveness cost of parallel groups worth a named limit.
5. bugs runs installed analyzers (ruff --no-cache, go vet) in the real tree for any role, outside the runner. They are read-only analyzers, not project code.
6. The runner records cwd "." for a run that ran in a temporary copy (the copy shows only in runner.executed and in the log).
7. eccode-gf's help text does not list "close accept", although the command exists (bin/eccode-gf.js:225) and the design names it.
8. OS-level isolation (L-GF-40) as already registered.
